claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To start, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. Their name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex!

To help determine your eligibility, could you please tell me how old Alex is?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Since Alex is 18, their eligibility depends on their current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- A traineeship in England

Or has Alex left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming Alex is studying for his A-levels.

Just a couple more questions to check eligibility:

Does Alex's A-level course involve more than 12 hours per week of supervised study or course-related work experience?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it does. It's a full-time course, so there's plenty of supervised study each week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One more important question: Is Alex's A-level course provided by an employer as part of a job contract, or is it a standard course at a school or college (not connected to employment)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's a standard course at college, not connected to any employment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just one final question: Are you responsible for Alex? This means that Alex lives with you, or you contribute to the cost of looking after him at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit you would receive.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I can now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- **Age**: Although Alex is 18, Child Benefit can continue until a child turns 20 if they remain in approved education or training.
- **Approved education**: A-levels are an approved form of education.
- **Course hours**: The course is full-time with more than 12 hours per week of supervised study, meeting the requirements.
- **Not employer-provided**: The course is a standard college course, not connected to employment.
- **Responsibility**: You are responsible for Alex as he lives with you.

Please note that you'll need to inform the Child Benefit Office if Alex's circumstances change, such as if he leaves education or starts working more than 24 hours a week.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
